title: The validator in front of every agent write
request: Make the workflow validator impossible to skip: every write tool declares the move it makes, the runtime asks studio.graph.check as the agent before the handler runs, and a refusal is logged and returned to the model with the reason and the rules. The Home agent's draft writes get their own checks.
spec: Each write tool declares its move (run_stage, set_solution, approve_gate, approve_stage, capture); a refusal is logged by graph.log and returned as the tool result with the reason and cited rules; a test enumerates the registry and fails if a write tool has no move; Home writes (record, set_pack, propose_workflow, simulate_data) get workflow validation, a pack list and one simulation at a time. Done when a test calls every write tool with a move the validator refuses and gets the reason and a logged transition, and no write tool bypasses the check.
plan: Read the validator (studio/graph.py) and list which project writes it checks; four (create_project, attach_data, set_settings, propose_solution) were never checked or logged.
Write the test first, as a new file while A2.1 was under review: refuse every project write tool and fail when a new write tool has no refusal case.

Make registration refuse a write tool without a move, and send every write through its scope's guard: the project guard asks graph.check as the agent; the draft guard checks the pack list and the user's choice, workflow.validate and one preparation at a time.
Add graph checks for the four uncovered writes (for example the agent may not replace the data under a solution the owner signed).
Run check-all and the review; fix the two findings; commit.

decisions.decision: The guard lives in the registry's call path, not in each handler.
decisions.why: A handler that checks the graph itself can be written without the check; a registry that refuses to run a write without a guard cannot be bypassed by a new tool.

decisions.decision: A refused Home workflow keeps the current workflow instead of falling back to the template.
decisions.why: Falling back silently replaced work the person had already seen with a generic template.

decisions.decision: The create_project transition logs the name but not the user's goal.
decisions.why: The goal is the user's free text and the transition log is the future training source (A6.1); the reviewer noted it would carry up to 300 characters of the task.

decisions.decision: create_project's refusal is returned but not logged.
decisions.why: Before a project exists there is no log to write to; the exception is written in the status row rather than hidden.

change: Registry refuses a write tool without a declared move and runs writes only through their scope's guard; the project guard calls studio.graph.check as the agent, logs a refusal as a transition and returns the reason, the failed checks and the rules; studio/graph.py gained checks for create_project, attach_data, set_settings and propose_solution; the draft guard checks set_pack, propose_workflow and simulate; tests/test_agents_validator.py.

findings.defect: A refused run_all now returned a flat result, and the intern's standard plan crashed on it.
findings.scenario: A project with data and a saved but unsigned solution, policy require_solution_signoff on, handed to the intern with no model: run_all returns {'error': ..., 'status': 'needs_approval'} at the top level; the report loops over the result expecting stage records and raises 'string indices must be integers'; the session ends failed instead of completing with a report naming the refusal. The same happens while a stage is running.
findings.cause: The guard returned its refusal directly, where before the engine's refusal came back keyed by stage.
findings.fix: In the run_all refusal branch, keep the old shape: the refusal keyed by the stage.
findings.test: The run_all case in tests/test_agents_validator.py reads result[stage].
findings.impact: A person who handed a project with an unsigned solution to the intern without a model would get a failed session with a Python TypeError instead of a report saying the owner must sign first: the refusal, the one useful answer, was lost.

findings.defect: The Home agent now refused model calls that left out a 'required' argument the handlers had always defaulted.
findings.scenario: request_data with no text, set_pack with a key but no why, ask_user with a question but no field, and record without field all worked before and now came back as 'Missing required argument'.
findings.cause: The registry's names-level check still enforced the schemas' required lists, which were stricter than the handlers.
findings.fix: The Home handlers keep defaulting what small models leave out (the defaults are filled before the registry check); A2.4 later made those keys optional in the schemas.
findings.test: Draft flow tests with the short calls.
findings.impact: Small models that leave out a defaulted key would have had ordinary Home calls refused (asking a question, offering data, choosing a pack), so the conversation stalled on 'Missing required argument' where it used to move on.
alternatives: Make those keys optional in the draft schemas, the reviewer's other option: deferred to A2.4, which moved the Home agent onto the full schema check and changed the schemas there.

findings.defect: An A2.1 test assumed only project tools have moves.
findings.scenario: With draft writes declaring moves, the test checked them against the project move list and failed.
findings.cause: The test was written when only one scope had writes.
findings.fix: Each move is checked against its own scope's list.
findings.impact: Nothing wrong reached a person; the stale assumption blocked the gate, and left as it was it would have checked every draft move against the project move list.

outcome: Done: a write tool cannot be registered without its move and a write in a scope without a guard never runs; project writes pass studio.graph.check as the agent; the four uncovered project writes are now checked and logged. The gate passed with 430 tests on files and on PostgreSQL and the four flows; two review findings fixed.
lessons: Moving a check to a new place can change the shape of a refusal; callers that parse the old shape break.
When a guard becomes mandatory, list the writes the old code never checked: here four, one of which let the agent replace data under a signed solution.
Do not log users' free text in a log that will become training data.
risks: A write tool registered without a declared move bypasses the validator entirely.
Moving refusals into the registry changes the shape of the result that callers such as the intern's report loop parse.
Project writes the old code never checked (create_project, attach_data, set_settings, propose_solution) could let the agent replace data under a signed solution.
Logging refusals puts the user's free text into the transition log, which later becomes training data.
The registry's names-level check refusing short calls the Home handlers always defaulted.
